result.summary: Do not dispatch yet: unlinking a symlinked state directory can erase the evidence needed to protect quarantined originals.

findings.title: Preserve shelf aliases across both disposal sweeps
findings.body: X1 step 0 unlinks a symlinked state before step 1 computes protected targets. With <core>/state pointing to <core>/logs and an original in logs/quarantine, this removes the alias without removing the original. X17 then derives anchors under the now-absent state path, so X18 permits recursively deleting logs and the original. This is reachable through the exported direct sweep or a link-and-preserve introduced after the CLI gate. Computing anchors before unlinking only protects the first sweep: uninstall.js calls the disposer again at line 467, when the alias is already gone. An in-memory model of both orderings confirmed this loss.
findings.recommendation: Amend X1/X18 to retain a state symlink when its target contains a protected shelf, so protection remains discoverable across sweeps and retries. Add direct-sweep and post-gate tests with state pointing to logs, asserting original bytes survive both live disposer calls.

next_steps: Close the alias-lifetime gap and rerun the design review.
